title: Can Global XAI Methods Reveal Injected Behaviours in LLMs? SHAP vs Rule Extraction vs RuleSHAP

problem.claim: The study investigates whether belief-driven heuristics behind misinformation-related behaviour can be recovered from black-box LLM behaviour as explicit rules.

gap.claim: Global rule-extraction methods in explainable AI are designed for numerical input-output data rather than text.

contributions.claim: The authors elicit global LLM beliefs and map them to numerical scores through statistically validated abstractions so off-the-shelf global XAI methods can detect belief-driven heuristics.
The authors propose RuleSHAP, which couples global SHAP aggregates with rule induction to capture non-univariate triggers.
The study evaluates detection of injected nonlinear behavioural triggers of increasing complexity in GPT-family and Llama models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: RuleFit often misses non-univariate triggers, while global SHAP better ranks conjunctive trigger features but does not yield symbolic rules.
RuleSHAP improves MRR@1 over RuleFit by an average of 82%.
The results suggest a practical pathway for surfacing behavioural triggers in LLMs.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs can amplify misinformation, including behaviours associated with valence framing, information overload, and oversimplification.
The study asks whether belief-driven heuristics behind misinformation-related behaviour can be recovered from black-box LLM behaviour as explicit rules.
Existing global rule-extraction methods are built for numerical input-output data rather than text.
The authors convert elicited global LLM beliefs into numerical scores, apply global XAI, and evaluate injected nonlinear triggers in GPT-family and Llama models.
RuleFit misses some non-univariate triggers, while RuleSHAP combines SHAP aggregates with rule induction and improves reported MRR@1 over RuleFit.

source_observation.claim: Global SHAP better ranks conjunctive trigger features but does not produce symbolic rules, while RuleSHAP combines SHAP aggregates with rule induction.

interpretation.claim: Combining feature-importance aggregation with explicit rule induction may help recover interactions that standalone rule extraction or attribution misses.

application.claim: For black-box model behavior analysis, use attribution methods to identify candidate interacting features and rule induction to express them symbolically.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the evaluated trigger types, GPT-family and Llama models, or reported settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation protocol, statistical validation details, or model versions.
The abstract does not report the absolute MRR@1 values or uncertainty estimates.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
